steps.say: An artifact, built in a chat. One click on Install as app.
Now it opens in its own window, with its own icon, like any other app on the desk.

scenes.headline: The web page as an app and a tool surface
scenes.sub: Claude's installable artifacts, and WebMCP in the AI SDK
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Trolley. Two launches on one evening, both about what a web page can be.

scenes.title: Three tiers of permission

items.say: By default an installed app can do only what a browser page can.
It can ask for more: notifications, global shortcuts, a menu bar item.
Or full access to run programs and change files. Claude asks again after every update, even your own edits.

scenes.say: What the app may touch is up to you.

steps.say: One person posted sixty-one apps made this way. A crystal plate scorer. A knitting chart.
A glacier traced year by year. A sailing passage with a tide gate. Each one a dense, single window.

scenes.title: Model on the server, tools in the tab

heads: The page lists its tools with every request
The result goes back, and the loop goes on

steps.say: The page registers its functions as tools on document model context. Before each request, the browser lists them and sends the definitions to your server.
steps.term: WebMCP: a page's functions as tools

steps.say: The model runs on the server, key and all. It answers with a tool call, but the server has no way to run it.
The browser does. The call goes through the MCP client and its WebMCP transport into the page's own function, and two mugs land in the cart.
The result goes back as structured content, and the chat sends itself again for the next step.
In the AI SDK it is one transport. Pass it the page's model context.
List the tools, call one. There is no server on the other end of this wire.
Add two mugs and a tote bag.
steps.caption: One act call, two quantities

steps.say: Clear the cart. Add three T-shirts and a mug.
Place the order. The page marked that button for a person, so it asks first.
No tool was written for any of it.

left.title: By hand, per site
items: one call can finish a checkout
left.say: WindTunnel's sites wrote their tools by hand: over seven thousand lines for forty-four tools. One of them finishes a whole checkout in a single call.

right.title: UI SDK's three
items: nothing to write, more to plan
right.say: UI SDK registers three generic tools for the whole page. Nothing to write, but the model plans every step from the labels.

scenes.text: An app needs permissions you can revoke; a tool surface needs an allow callback. The page now has both.
scenes.say: An installed app needs permissions you can take back. A page full of tools needs an allow callback. The same page can now have both.

recap: Install as app: a window, an icon, three tiers
WebMCP: the model on the server, tools in the tab
UI SDK: three tools for any page
scenes.say: A window and permissions from Claude. Tools in the tab through WebMCP. Three of them free from UI SDK.
